# Security and Login Requirements Checklist: QR Login and First-Run Setup

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and measurability of the QR credential-handling and setup-recovery requirements.
**Created**: 2026-09-25
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 - Does the specification define that the complete UTF-8 string `user;password;clienturl;managerurl` is Base64-encoded once, with `user` meaning username? [Completeness, Spec §Clarifications, §FR-002]
- [x] CHK002 - Are QR payloads with missing, empty, additional, or semicolon-containing fields explicitly covered by rejection requirements? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-003]
- [x] CHK003 - Are requirements defined for how the app handles a service being reachable while the other configured service is unavailable, including whether setup may partially succeed? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-007]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK004 - Are accepted Base64 alphabet, padding, whitespace, UTF-8 failure, and decoded field-count rules specific enough to produce interoperable QR codes? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002–003]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are permitted URL schemes and rules for hosts, embedded credentials, redirects, and plain-HTTP confirmation explicit? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK006 - Is it clear which service destinations are shown for confirmation and that no credentials are sent before confirmation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK007 - Are the QR encoding rule and manual-entry field requirements consistent about the four values and their meaning? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, §FR-005, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are the privacy warning and secret-handling requirements consistent across the QR scan, destination preview, authentication, retry, and error flows? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-009–010]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK009 - Are camera permission denial or revocation, scan cancellation, and switching to manual entry fully specified as recoverable first-run paths? [Coverage, Exception Flow, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-001, §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK010 - Are requirements defined for interrupted authentication, repeated scans, and retrying after rejected credentials or unavailable services without losing correctable non-secret values? [Coverage, Recovery Flow, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK011 - Does the specification define whether transient QR text and decoded credentials are discarded after cancel, failure, and success, beyond prohibiting logs and diagnostics? [Gap, Spec §FR-009]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK012 - Can the success criteria objectively distinguish valid four-field payloads from malformed Base64, invalid UTF-8, and wrong field counts before any sign-in request? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK013 - Does the no-secret-leak success criterion cover logs, diagnostics, and user-facing errors across scan, parse, network, and authentication failures? [Measurability, Coverage, Spec §SC-004, §FR-009]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK014 - Are the existing external QR producer, shared authentication/session behavior, and expected client-versus-manager URL roles documented well enough to establish compatibility? [Dependency, Assumption, Spec §FR-011, §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
